blockingIssues.description: `flux apps global-status --json` rebuilds its `items` array from the unfiltered persisted `computed` dataset, so expired apps can appear even when `--include-expired` is omitted.

`flux apps troubleshoot` flattens upstream `global_registry_unreachable` signals into `not_in_global_registry` / `flux_error`, so registry-failure cases lose their intended correlated troubleshooting status.

`deriveProgressSemantic` prefers a parsed JSON `status: success` over later error events, so mixed progress streams can surface false-success results; the same root cause also breaks `flux apps test-install` in `m4-app-runtime-debug-and-execution-commands`.
`flux apps generate-spec` parses `--cpu` as an integer >= 1, rejecting valid fractional Flux v8 CPU values such as `0.5`.
Thrown MCP verify-flow errors are converted into generic `flux_error` failures before CLI payload shaping, so explicit verify `status: error` is not preserved on real exception paths.

The finalize-only Git deploy contract suite asserts a redacted plaintext plan spec for private-repo enterprise flows, but the shipped runtime enterprise-encrypts compose/contacts and stores empty arrays plus an `enterprise` blob.
CLI launcher keep-alive allowlists omit `flux_build_message_to_sign`, so pretty generic tool calls can print interactive launcher URLs and then immediately unref the local launcher.

appliedUpdates.description: Updated `.factory/library/shared-runtime.md` with M4 scrutiny adapter gotchas covering unfiltered resource datasets, fractional CPU parsing, private-repo Git deploy enterprise plan artifacts, thrown-tool error/status handling, and launcher-producing tool inventories.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Clarify how workers should satisfy and document the 'write failing tests first' rule for transcript-auditable runs, including partial-diff/follow-up slices where tests and implementation land in the same patch.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Reviews for `m4-app-global-status-and-troubleshoot`, `m4-app-lifecycle-and-redeploy-commands`, and `m4-app-runtime-debug-and-execution-commands` all flagged that the first targeted test invocation appears after an `ApplyPatch`, while `m4-app-planning-pricing-and-spec-generation` had to record a deviation because the feature explicitly required auditing an existing partial diff.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Document exceptions for finalize-only audits and observability-hook-first fixes so workers can verify existing diffs or expose minimal test hooks before a meaningful failing test exists.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The pass review for `m4-finalize-shared-git-redaction-diff` and the fail review for `m4-fix-local-launcher-exit-for-one-shot-cli` both note that the current tests-first wording does not cleanly fit finalize-only audits or cases where small exported hooks are required before launcher behavior can be observed.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: When the finalize-only diff is primarily tests or contract notes, require comparison against the canonical runtime/MCP contract tests already on the branch before approving the slice.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The `m4-finalize-git-deploy-existing-diff` review found that the new CLI contract test drifted from the existing enterprise-plan behavior already asserted in `flux-mcp/test/uxTools.test.ts`, but the finalize worker transcript did not read those canonical tests.
